explanation: Given, 9 divisions of main scale are equal to 10 divisions of Vernier scale. i.e. 9 MSD = 10 VSD $⇒ {\text{VSD}}=\frac{9}{10} {\text{MSD}}$ ...(i) Size of 1 main scale division, 1 MSD = 1 mm Now, least count, LC = 1MSD − 1VSD ...(ii) Using Eqs. (i) and (ii), we get ${\text{LC}}=1 {\text{MSD}}-\frac{9}{10} {\text{MSD}}=\frac{1}{10} {\text{MSD}}=\frac{1}{10} {\text{mm}}$ While measuring the diameter of bob. Main Scale Reading, MSR = 10 mm Vernier Scale Reading, VSR = 8 Zero error, e = 0.04 cm Now, diameter, $d=[{\text{MSR}}+{\text{LC}} ×{\text{VSR}}]-{e}$ $=(10 {\text{mm}}+\frac{1}{10} ×8 {\text{mm}})-0.04 {\text{cm}}$ $=(10.8) {\text{mm}}-0.04 {\text{cm}}$ $=1.08 {\text{cm}}-0.04 {\text{cm}}=1.04 {\text{cm}}$ Radius, $r=\frac{d}{2}=\frac{1.04}{2} {\text{cm}}=0.52 {\text{cm}}=52 ×10^{-2} {\text{cm}}$ ∴ Correct answer is 52.

question_text: Which of the following is not a dimensionless quantity?
explanation: Relative magnetic permeability $(\μ_{r})$ It is the ratio of permeability of medium to the permeability of free space i.e., $\μ_{r}={\μ_{m}}/{\μ_{0}}$ As, it is a ratio of permeabilities. So, it is unitless and dimensionless quantity. Power factor $(\cos \ϕ)$ It is cosine of phase difference between alternating current and alternating voltage. Hence, it has only a numerical value, so it is also a unitless and dimensionless quantity. Permeability of free space $(\μ_{0})$ It is the ratio of magnetising field induction (B) to magnetising field intensity (H) i.e. $\μ_{0}=\frac{\text{B}}{\text{H}}$ $⇒ [\μ_{0}]=\frac{[\text{B}]}{[\text{H}]}$ ...(i) Since, $\text{H}=\text{nl}$ where, n = number of turns per unit length and I = current $∴ [\text{H}]=[\text{n}][\text{I}]$ $=[{\text{L}}^{-1}][{\text{A}}]=[{\text{AL}}^{-1}]$ We know that, force on a current carrying conductor in magnetic field B is given as F = IBl where, l = length of the conductor, B = magnetic field and I = current. $∴ \text{B}=\frac{\text{F}}{\text{II}}$ $⇒ [\text{B}]=\frac{[\text{F}]}{[\text{I}][\text{I}]}={[{\text{MLT}}^{-2}]}/{[{\text{A}}][{\text{L}}]}=[{\text{MT}}^{-2} {\text{A}}^{-1}]$ ∴From Eq. (i), we have $[\μ_{0}]={[{\text{MT}}^{-2}{\text{A}}^{-1}]}/{[{\text{AL}}^{-1}]}=[{\text{MLT}}^{-2} {\text{A}}^{-2}]$ Hence, permeability of free space is not a dimensionless quantity. Quality factor It is the ratio of energy stored to the energy dissipated per cycle. Quality factor $={{ \text{Energy} \text{stored} }}/{{ \text{Energy} \text{dissipated} \text{per} c\text{ycle} }}$ As, it is ratio of energies so, it will be unitless and dimensionless quantity.

explanation: Magnetic induction Magnetic force of induction can be given as $\text{F}=\text{q} \text{v} \text{B}$ ⇒ $\text{B}=\frac{\text{F}}{q v}$ $[\text{B}]=\frac{[\text{F}]}{[q][v]}={[\text{M} \text{L} \text{T}^{-2}]}/{[{\text{AT}}][{\text{LT}}^{-1}]}=[{\text{M}}^{1} {\text{T}}^{-2} {\text{A}}^{-1}]$ Magnetic Flux Magnetic flux is the product of magnetic inductionand area. ϕ = B ⋅ A $[\ϕ]=[\text{B}][\text{A}]=[\text{M}^{1} \text{T}^{-2} \text{A}^{-1}][\text{L}^{2}]$ $=[\text{M} \text{L}^{2} \text{T}^{-2} \text{A}^{-1}]$ Magnetic permeability We know that, magnetic field inside the solenoid. $\text{B}=\μ_{0} \text{n} \text{I}$ ⇒ $\μ_{0}=\frac{\text{B}}{n l}$ (where, n is number of turns per unit length) $⇒ [\μ_{0}]=\frac{[\text{B}]}{[n][l]}={[\text{M} \text{T}^{-2} \text{A}^{-1}]}/{[\text{L}^{-1}][\text{A}]}=[\text{M} \text{L} \text{T}^{-2} \text{A}^{-2}]$ Magnetisation The magnetic dipole moment acquired per unitvolume is known as magnetisation. ${\text{I}}={{\text{M}}}/{{\text{V}}}$ $[\text{l}]={[{\text{L}}^{2} {\text{A}}]}/{[{\text{L}}^{3}]}=[{\text{L}}^{-1} {\text{A}}]$ Hence, no option is correct.

question_text: If the length of the pendulum in pendulum clock increases by $0.1 \%$, then the error in time per day is
explanation: Increase in length of pendulum is 0.1%. i.e. $\frac{\Δ\text{L}}{\text{L}} ×100=0.1$ Time period of pendulum is given by $\text{T}=2 \π\\sqrt{\frac{\text{L}}{g}}$ Here, 2 π and g are constant. $\frac{\Δ\text{T}}{\text{T}} ×100=\frac{1}{2} \frac{\Δ\text{L}}{\text{L}} ×100$ $⇒ \frac{\Δ\text{T}}{\text{T}} ×100=\frac{1}{2} ×0.1$ $\Δ\text{T}=0.05 ×\frac{\text{T}}{100}$ In one single day, the time in seconds is $\text{T}=24 ×60 ×60=86400 {\text{s}}$ $∴ \Δ\text{T}=0.05 ×\frac{86400}{100}=43.2 {\text{s}}$ Thus, the error in time per day is 43.2 s.

question_text: The acceleration due to gravity is found upto an accuracy of $4 \%$ on a planet. The energy supplied to a simple pendulum to known mass m to undertake oscillations of time period T is being estimated. If time period is measured to an accuracy of $3 \%$, the accuracy to which E is known as ..........%.
explanation: Given, accuracy of acceleration due to gravity = 4% Accuracy of time period = 3% Energy stored in pendulum at any instant is given as $\text{E}={\text{mgL} \θ^{2}}/{2}$ ...(i) Time period of pendulum is given by expression $\text{T}=2 \π\\sqrt{\frac{\text{L}}{g}}$ Rearrange the above expression for L, we get $\text{L}=g(\frac{\text{T}}{2 \π})^{2}$ ...(ii) Substituting the value of L in Eq. (i), we get $\text{E}={m g^{2} \θ^{2}}/{2}({\text{T}}{2 \π})^{2}={m g^{2} \θ^{2} \text{T}^{2}}/{8 \π^{2}}$ Now, the accuracy in measurement of energy can be calculated as $\frac{\Δ\text{E}}{\text{E}} ×100=2 \frac{\Δg}{g} ×100+2 \frac{\Δ\text{T}}{\text{T}} ×100$ (∵ m,θ and π are constant) ⇒ $\frac{\Δ\text{E}}{\text{E}} ×100=2 ×4 \%+2 ×3 \%=14 \%$ Thus, the accuracy to which E is known is 14%.

question_text: In a screw gauge, 5th division of the circular scale coincides with the reference line when the ratchet is closed. There are 50 divisions on the circular scale, and the main scale moves by $0.5 {\text{mm}}$ on a complete rotation. For a particular observation the reading on the main scale is $5 {\text{mm}}$ and the 20th division of the circular scale coincides with reference line. Calculate the true reading.
explanation: Least count of a screw gauge is given by Least count $(\text{LC})={{ \text{Pitch} }}/{{ \text{Number} \text{of} \text{circular} \text{scale} \text{divisions} }}$ $⇒ {\text{LC}}=\frac{0.5}{50}$ ...(i) The actual reading (true reading) = Main scale reading + Least count × Circular division − Zero error $=5+(\frac{0.5}{50}) ×20-\frac{0.5}{50} ×5$ [∴ Zero error = Least count × Coinciding division] $=5+\frac{0.5}{50}(20-5)$ $=5+\frac{0.5}{50}(15)$ $=5+\frac{15}{100}$ $=\frac{515}{100} {\text{mm}}=5.15 {\text{mm}}$
